request.spec:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
ROLLUP and TOTALS lines now end with `overdue-total=…`, and a change that moves only an overdue-total now writes them too. All 4 Playwright tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The whole change is on the server's audit side, in `rollup/Rollup.java` and `rollup/Rollups.java`; the front end already showed overdue totals, so it didn't need touching.

- **ROLLUP line:** a person's overdue-total adds up the dues of their overdue claims (shown with the late charge), leaving out `n/a`. A claim is included only if it already counts toward that person's figures. This matches what the screen shows in `person-overdue-total`.
- **TOTALS line:** the sheet's overdue-total is every person's added together.
- **When lines are written:** a person's ROLLUP line now appears when their claimed, due-total or overdue-total changes, and a TOTALS line when any of the three totals changes.
- **Changing today:** setting the sheet's today already recorded rollup lines, so a new today that makes a claim overdue, or stops one being overdue, now writes them even when no due moved.

The new field is added at the end of each line and the existing fields keep their order.
